call_points.text: Bespoke loan book guided to grow 15-20% YoY; about half that growth was achieved in Q1.
Wealth net flows targeted at about ₹6,000 Cr minimum for the year; Q1 net flows were about ₹2,000 Cr.
ROE expected in a similar range or better than last year's 11.5%; mid-to-high teens only once Wealth and AMC scale.
July transaction revenue in Corporate Advisory and Capital Markets already exceeded June's.
Wealth employee costs have peaked; hiring will be selective and judicious going forward.
Group debt-to-equity is 0.8x, down from 1.9x in FY24; management expects it back near 2x within three years.
ARC resolutions are lumpy; income is booked when resolution happens, so quarterly revenue can swing.
Demerger or separate listing of Wealth and Asset Management only once it is larger; no timeline given.
Private Markets loan book guided to ₹5,000 Cr by March 2027, 15-20% growth.
Management expects the pipeline to nearly double YoY by September-October 2026.
Committed to declaring 50% of PAT as dividend every year.
Real estate lending returns still not attractive; growth to come from corporate loans instead.

guidance.statement: Targets 15% revenue growth and 15% ROE at the end of the investment cycle
Private Markets standard loan book to reach about ₹5,000 Cr by March 2027, 15-20% growth
Wealth Management to grow 20-25% in FY27, about ₹6,000 Cr of inflows
Affordable home loans AUM to grow 25% YoY; IPO targeted for 2028-29
Private Markets recovery of ₹250-300 Cr in FY27
Committed to declaring 50% of PAT as dividend every year
Bespoke loan book to grow at least 15-20% YoY
Wealth net flows targeted at about ₹6,000 Cr minimum for the year
Further ₹150 Cr investment in Asset Management over the next 2-3 years
ARC to be debt-free within six months
Group debt-to-equity to return to about 2x within three years

operating_notes.text: IPO pipeline of ₹1,40,000 Cr with 55 IPO documents filed; management expects the pipeline to nearly double YoY by September-October 2026.
Private Markets book at March 2026: ₹2,685 Cr corporate loans, ₹1,100 Cr real estate, ₹228 Cr non-core, ₹3,665 Cr distressed credit and ₹3,000 Cr cash.
Affordable home loans gross NPA 0.5% and collection efficiency 99.4% at March 31, 2026, on AUM of ₹3,460 Cr.
ARC gross resolutions were over ₹2,000 Cr in Q1FY27, of which the group's share of cash flows was over ₹1,200 Cr.
Distressed credit book was ₹3,114 Cr at Q1FY27, down from ₹3,665 Cr at Q4FY26 after ₹1,200 Cr recovery and ₹600 Cr new deployment.
Wealth loan book grew 43% YoY to ₹2,417 Cr; recurring AUM was about ₹33,400 Cr, 30% of total AUM.

timeline.summary: On its 1 June 2026 Q4FY26 call, JM Financial reported FY26 PAT of ₹1,202 Cr, up 46% YoY, and guided to 15% revenue growth and 15% ROE, with a ₹1,40,000 Cr IPO pipeline.

On its 4 August 2026 Q1FY27 call, JM Financial reported net revenue up 13% YoY to ₹883 Cr and flat reported PAT of ₹292 Cr, with Private Markets revenue doubling to ₹462 Cr on ARC recoveries while capital markets and wealth lagged.
